messages.subject: versions of Windows/Linux/Mac to test + 32/64-bit?
parts:
Daniel has virtual servers up and running
on the same Windows box as Jenkins.

Windows
-------
Daniel tested that things work in Windows XP
and Windows 7. We know Windows 8 is imminent
and should also be tested. We were going to skip
Vista.


Linux
-----
Daniel also validated that Stan works on Ubuntu Linux

Are there other versions of Linux we should test?
Debian, perhaps?


Mac
---
We know things work on Snow Leopard and Lion.
We should probably test Mountain Lion.

I can upgrade my own notebook to do that.


32- and 64-bit?
---------------
So far, all these tests have been on 64-bit machines.

Should we also test 32-bit versions? I'm imagining there
may be users other than my mom with 32-bit OSes.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: versions of Windows/Linux/Mac to test + 32/64-bit?
parts:
On Monday, August 27, 2012 6:32:18 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Are there other versions of Linux we should test?
Debian, perhaps?

If we were going to spend the effort to test another Linux distribution, it should be in the Red Hat family rather than the Debian family. My laptop is Debian, so we are covered there, but anything that works on either Debian or Ubuntu should also work on the other. For a library like Stan, I doubt there would be problems on any Linux distribution that supports the dependencies we need. Also, the versions we should test should be the "Long Term Support" or "Stable" versions, which are more likely to be installed on servers.

32- and 64-bit?
---------------
So far, all these tests have been on 64-bit machines.

Should we also test 32-bit versions?  I'm imagining there
may be users other than my mom with 32-bit OSes.

This is probably more of a CRAN issue than a genuine issue. We need rstan to build on 32bit PPA and 32bit Windows.

Ben

For the cpp files, previously I have a Makevar and Makevar.win, in which case both 32 and 64 bits are built on windows and Mac during installing from source.  But in order to have -O3 and not have -g, I am using Makefile and Makefile.win, in which case only one architecture is built when installing the package from source.  Is that an issue?
